foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.value: A graduate of a medical school outside the US and Canada must: (1) graduate from a school whose curriculum meets requirements for an unapproved medical school as determined by a committee selected by the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board; (2) successfully complete at least two years of approved graduate medical training in the US or Canada; (3) hold a valid certificate issued by the Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates (ECFMG); and (4) be able to communicate in English.

opioid_prescribing_limits.value: A physician may delegate the prescribing or ordering of a controlled substance listed in Schedule III, IV, or V only if the prescription (including refills) is for a period not to exceed 90 days. Delegation of Schedule II prescribing is limited to hospital facility-based practice or hospice care. Physicians must follow board guidelines for opioid antagonist prescribing.
opioid_prescribing_limits.quote: the prescription, including a refill of the prescription, is for a period not to exceed 90 days

pain_management_clinic_registration_requ.quote: A pain management clinic may not operate in this state unless the clinic is certified under this chapter.

telehealth_prescribing_rules.value: A physician may prescribe via telemedicine if a valid practitioner-patient relationship exists. This requires either a preexisting relationship, a call coverage arrangement, or synchronous audiovisual interaction or asynchronous store-and-forward with access to relevant clinical information. A practitioner-patient relationship is not present if prescribing an abortifacient or drug to terminate a pregnancy. Physicians must provide follow-up guidance and share records with the patient's primary care physician.
telehealth_prescribing_rules.quote: For purposes of Section 562.056, a valid practitioner-patient relationship is present between a practitioner providing a telemedicine medical service or a teledentistry dental service and a patient receiving the service as long as the practitioner complies with the standard of care described in Section 111.007
telehealth_prescribing_rules.citation: [UMBRELLA / Subtitle A - Provisions Applying to Health Professions Gener] Section 111.005

telemedicine_license_available.quote: A person who is physically located in another jurisdiction but who, through the use of any medium, including an electronic medium, performs an act that is part of a patient care service initiated in this state... is considered to be engaged in the practice of medicine in this state and is subject to appropriate regulation by the board.

interstate_medical_licensure_compact_mem.quote: the member states of the Interstate Medical Licensure Compact have allied in common purpose to develop a comprehensive process that complements the existing licensing and regulatory authority of state medical boards and provides a streamlined process that allows physicians to become licensed in multiple states

physician_assistant_supervision_model.quote: A physician may delegate to an advanced practice registered nurse or physician assistant, acting under adequate physician supervision, the act of prescribing or ordering a drug or device as authorized through a prescriptive authority agreement between the physician and the advanced practice registered nurse or physician assistant

physician_assistant_prescriptive_authori.value: A physician may delegate prescribing of nonprescription drugs, dangerous drugs, and controlled substances in Schedules III-V (for up to 90 days per prescription). Schedule II controlled substances may only be delegated in hospital facility-based practice or for hospice patients. The combined number of APRNs and PAs to whom a physician may delegate prescriptive authority generally may not exceed seven (with exceptions for medically underserved populations and facility-based practices).
physician_assistant_prescriptive_authori.quote: A physician's authority to delegate the prescribing or ordering of a drug or device under this subchapter is limited to: (1) nonprescription drugs; (2) dangerous drugs; and (3) controlled substances to the extent provided by Subsections (b) and (b-1).

max_physician_assistants_per_supervising.quote: the combined number of advanced practice registered nurses and physician assistants with whom a physician may enter into a prescriptive authority agreement may not exceed seven advanced practice registered nurses and physician assistants or the full-time equivalent of seven advanced practice registered nurses and physician assistants
